definitions.explanation: A word adopted from another language. In Japanese linguistics, this term covers words borrowed from any foreign language, including English, Portuguese, Dutch, Chinese, and others.

examples.japanese: 「パン」はポルトガル{語|ご}からの{借用語|しゃくようご}だ。
{日本語|にほんご}には{英語|えいご}からの{借用語|しゃくようご}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Japanese has many loanwords from English.

examples.japanese: {借用語|しゃくようご}は{元|もと}の{言語|げんご}とは{意味|いみ}が{変|か}わることがある。
examples.english: Loanwords sometimes change in meaning from their original language.

notes: A linguistics term composed of {借用|しゃくよう} (borrowing) + {語|ご} (word/language). In Japanese, loanwords are typically written in katakana and called {外来語|がいらいご}. Strictly speaking, {借用語|しゃくようご} is a broader academic term that includes {漢語|かんご} (Sino-Japanese words), while {外来語|がいらいご} usually refers to non-Chinese foreign words. Related terms: {和語|わご} (native Japanese words), {漢語|かんご} (Sino-Japanese words), {和製英語|わせいえいご} (Japanese-coined English words).
